text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistan believes the Afghan people's interests would be best served if there were no further military action against forces ready for talks on forming a broad-based government.

- Pakistan said an understanding had been reached with the IMF on the main elements of economic stabilisation and structural reforms but did not mention restoration of the suspended $600 million standby loan package.

- Pakistan roared into the final of the Four Nations tournament, beating Sri Lanka by 82 runs thanks to 16-year-old Shahid Afridi, who hit 100 off 37 balls -- the fastest century compiled in a one-day international.
- The World Bank has listed Pakistan among its three most corrupt borrowers and has ordered surprise raids by special squads to audit Bank-funded projects in these countries.
- Moody's Investors Service, a U.S. credit rating agency, has told Pakistan that its long-term credit rating for foreign currency would be reviewed, with a downgrade possible.
- The Collectorate of Central Excise asked the Commerce Ministry to fix minimum selling prices for beverages to stop a cut-throat price war between Coca Cola and Pepsi.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto left on Friday morning for London en route to Pakistan after a four-day stay in New York.

- The Karachi Stock Exchange commenced trading on a Friday after 19 years, but the day's rally ran out of steam as base shares and investment stocks received heavy battering on news reports that talks between Pakistan and the IMF had stalled.
